The first spark.

Published Friday, October 30, 2026

Data center costs, semiconductor investment and the networks supporting AI.

Download newsletter image

In this issue

Read the summaries and open the original articles below.

T&T Data Center Cost Index

The 2026–27 index covers 62 markets and 500+ projects. U.S. AI-ready facilities carry a construction premium of about 10%; cooling, density and labor affect comparisons.

Read the whole article ↗

SpaceX’s $119B Terafab Plans

SpaceX’s Terafab plans call for up to $119B in phased investment in Texas through 2036. The campus would include cleanrooms, onsite power and water systems; later phases remain conditional.

Read the whole article ↗

Verizon’s $2B-Plus AWS Deal

Verizon’s $2B-plus AWS deal supports distributed AI compute, fiber and edge sites. The agreement highlights demand for fiber connectivity and network hubs that bring AI computing closer to users.

Read the whole article ↗

NVIDIA and Nokia’s AI Networks

NVIDIA and Nokia are bringing AI computing to data centers, metro sites and cell sites. T-Mobile has completed a commercial AI-RAN call; other operators are preparing live trials.

Read the whole article ↗

The TMT Spark ecosystem

Thirteen industries. One conversation.

TMT no longer stops at technology, media and telecom. Compute needs power, power needs construction, construction needs capital — and all of it lands in real estate. Spark exists to put those groups in the same room. Select a node to explore.

TMT Spark

Every Spark conversation crosses at least two of these industries — that's the point. Cross-industry rooms surface the constraints and opportunities no single-sector event can see.

About TMT Spark

Educate first. Build relationships second. Business follows naturally.

TMT Spark is how Turner & Townsend's Technology, Media & Telecommunications practice shows up in the industry — as a publisher, a convener and a community rather than a cold caller. Instead of approaching prospective clients with a sales message, Spark invites industry leaders into conversations about where the industry is going. The public experience is media and education. What follows is relationships.

"The conversation comes before the pitch."
Internal view — how Spark supports Turner & Townsend's TMT strategy

The TMT Spark network effect

Two ways to meet an executive.

The platform doesn't replace business development — it replaces the cold open. Compare the paths.

Traditional outreach

1

Cold email. "Can Turner & Townsend help you manage your next construction project?"

2

Sales meeting request. A calendar invite from someone they've never met.

3

Low response rate. The message competes with every other vendor in the inbox.

Transactional from the first word — and easy to ignore.

The TMT Spark approach

1

Industry research. Spark's editorial work surfaces who is building, expanding and investing.

2

Invite them onto TMT Spark. A panel, a roundtable, an interview — a reason to talk that isn't a pitch.

3

Discuss their expertise. The conversation is about their world: their constraints, their plans, their view of the market.

4

Build the relationship. Shared interests, real content, follow-ups that feel natural.

5

Understand their priorities. Growth plans, cost pressures, infrastructure constraints — heard firsthand.

6

Introduce Turner & Townsend capabilities when appropriate. Only where Turner & Townsend can actually help — and only when the timing is right.

Reciprocal from the first word — and worth responding to.
" A technology executive may not respond to

"Can we sell you cost management services?"

A pitch with nothing in it for them. Deleted in seconds.

" But they may respond to

"We're interviewing leaders about how AI companies are managing the infrastructure constraints created by rapid growth. We'd love your perspective."

An invitation to be the expert. That conversation creates a genuine relationship.

What conversations surface

Listening is the intelligence engine.

In session transcripts, roundtables and interviews, Turner & Townsend teams hear — directly and unprompted — the things a cold call never reaches:

Industry challengesCapital investment plansExpansion plans Infrastructure constraintsConstruction challengesCost pressures Power constraintsTalent challengesReal estate needs Data center strategiesNew technologiesUpcoming projects

A relationship, step by step

From invitation to opportunity.

One illustrative journey from invitation to opportunity.

AI

Example AI Company

VP of Real Estate · 900 → 2,400 employees in 18 months

Illustrative
Step 1 · Signal

Spark spots the growth

Industry research for the newsletter flags the company's rapid hiring and a new funding round. No outreach yet — just editorial attention.

Step 2 · Invitation

An invitation, not a pitch

The VP of Real Estate is invited into a TMT Spark Live conversation: "How AI Companies Are Rethinking the Workplace."

Step 3 · Conversation

They talk about their world

On the record, the executive shares what growth actually feels like:

Rapid employee growthNew office requirementsConstruction schedulesBudget uncertaintyScaling across multiple cities
Step 4 · Understanding

Turner & Townsend hears where it could help

Listening — not selling — reveals where the company may need support and helps the team understand what matters most:

Cost managementProgram managementWorkplace deliveryProcurement strategy
Step 5 · Relationship

The relationship continues naturally

The session recap publishes in the next edition and the executive shares it. They join the next roundtable, meet Turner & Townsend specialists in the room, and keep the conversation going — because it's useful to them.

Step 6 · Opportunity

The conversation becomes an opportunity

When the expansion plan firms up, the company already knows — and trusts — the Turner & Townsend team. The conversation potentially becomes a business opportunity, on the client's timeline.

TMT Spark is not designed to turn every conversation into a sales lead. Its value comes from building a trusted industry network. Opportunities are a natural byproduct of that network.
